changes: pads: none → pads (groove_mm 0, lip_mm 0, pad_angle_deg 28, pad_tpu_mm 2, reach_mm 5, width_mm 12)
why: This is the more conservative variant for the held small objects. At 17-35 mm the moving pad is tilted only about -8 to -14 deg instead of about -21 deg, so dice and the marker are less disturbed. It fully fixes potted meat. It may fix tuna (tip rise about +17 mm at 85 mm), but probably not pudding or sugar. Kept only if it gains and holds everything.

Reach is the only pads parameter never taken past 7.3 mm. The only evidence that it changes wide-object outcomes is that b000 at 45 deg lost all three gains when reach dropped to 1.5 mm. Pad angle cannot be raised without losing banana: 37, 41 and 45 all did, at every reach, width and TPU tried. So longer reach at the banana-safe 28 deg is the last cheap lever. If grasp depth is set relative to the stock fingertip, 6 mm more reach puts both tips 6 mm deeper. That brings the moving tip (+11 to +17 mm for pudding at 70-78 mm) below the 38 mm top. If depth is set relative to the actual tips, this changes nothing, and the trial settles that question for $0. A swap is not justified: the slides skip teeth past about 55 mm and the parallelogram rises +54 mm at 85 mm.

Continue the one pads direction that has gained without loss: reach 11 → 17 mm, with angle 28°, TPU 2 mm and width 12 mm unchanged. The brief shows reach barely changes the fingertip geometry: the moving tip at 85 mm is +21 mm with reach 11 and +23 mm with bare faces. So every held object keeps its 28° face behaviour (parallel at 45 mm, −2 mm tip at 17–25 mm). Only the length of gripping surface below the stock tip changes. Cheaper moves are used up: 28° with any width or TPU gains nothing, and every angle ≥37° loses banana. I stop at 17 mm rather than 30 mm, so the longer pad's tip, swung in by 17° or more near the closed jaw, does not run into the fixed pad (the interference that got the groove variant refused).

This is the low end of the untested range from 28 to 37 deg, and the first pad angle above 28 tried at reach 17. 37, 41 and 45 all lost banana at t=0.02 s; 28 holds it. A 3 deg step should keep banana clear while trimming about 2 deg of tilt and 1 mm of tip rise at 85-96 mm. It is mainly a bracket point on where banana breaks. If it holds everything and gains even one wide box, the next step continues from here. Swaps cannot do this: every jaw except the hinge reaches only 48-88 mm, and the 12 V servos cost $68 against $40 left.
